sanskrit: tam uvācottaṅkaḥ gurvarthe kuṇḍalābhyām arthy āgato 'smīti ye te kṣatriyayā pinaddhe kuṇḍale te bhavān dātum arhatīti
english: Uttaṅka spoke to him: 'I have come seeking the earrings for the sake of my teacher. Those earrings that the queen wears — you ought to give them to me.'

sanskrit: taṃ pauṣyaḥ pratyuvāca praviśyāntaḥpuraṃ kṣatriyā yācyatām iti
english: Pauṣya replied to him: 'Enter the inner apartments and ask the queen herself.'

sanskrit: sa tenaivam uktaḥ praviśyāntaḥpuraṃ kṣatriyāṃ nāpaśyat
english: Told thus, he entered the inner apartments but did not see the queen.

sanskrit: sa pauṣyaṃ punar uvāca na yuktaṃ bhavatā vayam anṛtenopacaritum na hi te kṣatriyāntaḥpure saṃnihitā naināṃ paśyāmīti
english: He said to Pauṣya again: 'It is not right of you to deal with me falsely. The queen is not present in your inner apartments — I do not see her.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktaḥ pauṣyas taṃ pratyuvāca saṃprati bhavān ucchiṣṭaḥ smara tāvat na hi sā kṣatriyā ucchiṣṭenāśucinā vā śakyā draṣṭum pativratātvād eṣā nāśucer darśanam upaitīti
english: Pauṣya, addressed thus, replied to him: 'Consider first whether you are in a state of having eaten without performing the ritual rinsing. The queen cannot be seen by one who has eaten and is impure; being a devoted wife, she does not come before the sight of one who is unclean.'

sanskrit: athaivam ukta uttaṅkaḥ smṛtvovāca asti khalu mayocchiṣṭenopaspṛṣṭaṃ śīghraṃ gacchatā ceti
english: Addressed thus, Uttaṅka reflected and said: 'It is true — I did touch water while in a state of ritual impurity after eating, since I was walking hurriedly.'

sanskrit: taṃ pauṣyaḥ pratyuvāca etat tad evaṃ hi na gacchatopaspṛṣṭaṃ bhavati na sthiteneti
english: Pauṣya replied to him: 'That is indeed so — water touched while walking does not count as the proper ritual contact; it must be done while seated still.'

sanskrit: athottaṅkas tathety uktvā prāṅmukha upaviśya suprakṣālitapāṇipādavadano 'śabdābhir hṛdayaṃgamābhir adbhir upaspṛśya triḥ pītvā dviḥ parimṛjya khāny adbhir upaspṛśyāntaḥpuraṃ praviśya tāṃ kṣatriyām apaśyat
english: Then Uttaṅka, saying 'so be it,' sat facing east; with hands, feet, and face thoroughly washed, he performed the water-ritual with water that was soundless and pleasing to the heart — drinking three times and wiping twice — and then touched the orifices of the body with water. He entered the inner apartments and beheld the queen.

sanskrit: sā ca dṛṣṭvaivottaṅkam abhyutthāyābhivādyovāca svāgataṃ te bhagavan ājñāpaya kiṃ karavāṇīti
english: And she, upon seeing Uttaṅka, rose to receive him, offered him reverence and said: 'Welcome, venerable one. Command me — what shall I do?'

sanskrit: sa tām uvāca ete kuṇḍale gurvarthaṃ me bhikṣite dātum arhasīti
english: He said to her: 'These earrings have been requested by me for the sake of my teacher — please bestow them.'

sanskrit: sā prītā tena tasya sadbhāvena pātram ayam anatikramaṇīyaś ceti matvā te kuṇḍale avamucyāsmai prāyacchat
english: She, pleased by that sincerity of his, thinking 'this man is a worthy recipient and one whose request cannot be refused,' removed the earrings and gave them to him.

sanskrit: āha cainam ete kuṇḍale takṣako nāgarājaḥ prārthayati apramatto netum arhasīti
english: And she said to him: 'Takṣaka, the king of the serpents, covets these earrings — carry them away with vigilance.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktas tāṃ kṣatriyāṃ pratyuvāca bhavati sunirvṛtā bhava na māṃ śaktas takṣako nāgarājo dharṣayitum iti
english: Addressed thus, he replied to the queen: 'Be at ease, my lady. Takṣaka, the king of the serpents, is not able to assail me.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktvā tāṃ kṣatriyām āmantrya pauṣyasakāśam āgacchat
english: Having spoken thus and taken leave of the queen, he returned to where Pauṣya was.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvovāca bhoḥ pauṣya prīto 'smīti
english: Seeing him, he said: 'I am pleased, O Pauṣya.'

sanskrit: taṃ pauṣyaḥ pratyuvāca bhagavaṃś cirasya pātram āsādyate bhavāṃś ca guṇavān atithiḥ tat kariṣye śrāddham kṣaṇaḥ kriyatām iti
english: Pauṣya replied to him: 'Reverend sir, a worthy recipient is encountered only after a long time, and you are a guest endowed with virtues. I shall perform the ancestral śrāddha ceremony — please wait a moment.'

sanskrit: tam uttaṅkaḥ pratyuvāca kṛtakṣaṇa evāsmi śīghram icchāmi yathopapannam annam upahṛtaṃ bhavateti
english: Uttaṅka replied to him: 'The moment is already set for me — I wish whatever food is readily available to be served quickly.'

sanskrit: sa tathety uktvā yathopapannenānnenainaṃ bhojayām āsa
english: He said 'so be it' and fed him with whatever food was at hand.

sanskrit: athottaṅkaḥ śītam annaṃ sakeśaṃ dṛṣṭvā aśucy etad iti matvā pauṣyam uvāca yasmān me aśucy annaṃ dadāsi tasmad andho bhaviṣyasīti
english: But Uttaṅka, seeing the food was cold and contained a hair, considered it impure and said to Pauṣya: 'Since you give me impure food, you shall become blind.'

sanskrit: taṃ pauṣyaḥ pratyuvāca yasmāt tvam apy aduṣṭam annaṃ dūṣayasi tasmād anapatyo bhaviṣyasīti
english: Pauṣya replied to him: 'Since you too condemn food that is not defiled, you shall be without offspring.'

sanskrit: so 'tha pauṣyas tasyāśucibhāvam annasyāgamayām āsa
english: Then Pauṣya proved the impure state of the food.

sanskrit: atha tadannaṃ muktakeśyā striyopahṛtaṃ sakeśam aśuci matvottaṅkaṃ prasādayām āsa bhagavann ajñānād etad annaṃ sakeśam upahṛtaṃ śītaṃ ca tat kṣāmaye bhavantam na bhaveyam andha iti
english: Then, the food having been brought by a woman with loosened hair, and being found to contain hair and to be cold and impure, he sought to appease Uttaṅka: 'Reverend sir, through ignorance this food was brought to you with hair in it and cold. I beg your forgiveness — may I not become blind.'

sanskrit: tam uttaṅkaḥ pratyuvāca na mṛṣā bravīmi bhūtvā tvam andho nacirād anandho bhaviṣyasīti mamāpi śāpo na bhaved bhavatā datta iti
english: Uttaṅka replied to him: 'I do not speak falsely — you shall become blind and before long become sighted again. And let the curse you have uttered upon me also not come to pass.'

sanskrit: taṃ pauṣyaḥ pratyuvāca nāhaṃ śaktaḥ śāpaṃ pratyādātum na hi me manyur adyāpy upaśamaṃ gacchati kiṃ caitad bhavatā na jñāyate yathā
english: Pauṣya replied to him: 'I am not able to take back the curse, for my anger has not yet subsided. Moreover, do you not know this truth —'

sanskrit: nāvanītaṃ hṛdayaṃ brāhmaṇasya; vāci kṣuro nihitas tīkṣṇadhāraḥ viparītam etad ubhayaṃ kṣatriyasya; vāṅ nāvanītī hṛdayaṃ tīkṣṇadhāram
english: 'The heart of a brahmin is soft as butter, yet on his tongue is placed a razor sharp-edged. The opposite holds for the warrior: his speech is not soft as butter, but his heart is keen-edged.'

sanskrit: iti tad evaṃ gate na śakto 'haṃ tīkṣṇahṛdayatvāt taṃ śāpam anyathā kartum gamyatām iti
english: 'Thus being so, I am not able to undo that curse, for my heart is sharp. Go your way.'

sanskrit: tam uttaṅkaḥ pratyuvāca bhavatāham annasyāśucibhāvam āgamayya pratyanunītaḥ prāk ca te 'bhihitam yasmād aduṣṭam annaṃ dūṣayasi tasmād anapatyo bhaviṣyasīti duṣṭe cānne naiṣa mama śāpo bhaviṣyatīti
english: Uttaṅka replied to him: 'I have been shown the impure state of the food by you and have been propitiated. Yet earlier you said to me: "Since you condemn food that is not defiled, you shall be without offspring." Since the food was indeed defiled, this curse of mine shall not take effect.'

sanskrit: sādhayāmas tāvad ity uktvā prātiṣṭhatottaṅkas te kuṇḍale gṛhītvā
english: Saying 'Let us now complete our task,' Uttaṅka departed, taking the earrings with him.

sanskrit: so 'paśyat pathi nagnaṃ śramaṇam āgacchantaṃ muhur muhur dṛśyamānam adṛśyamānaṃ ca athottaṅkas te kuṇḍale bhūmau nikṣipyodakārthaṃ pracakrame
english: On the path he saw a naked mendicant approaching, appearing and disappearing again and again. Then Uttaṅka set those earrings down on the ground and went in search of water.

sanskrit: etasminn antare sa śramaṇas tvaramāṇa upasṛtya te kuṇḍale gṛhītvā prādravat tam uttaṅko 'bhisṛtya jagrāha sa tad rūpaṃ vihāya takṣakarūpaṃ kṛtvā sahasā dharaṇyāṃ vivṛtaṃ mahābilaṃ viveśa
english: In that interval, the mendicant swiftly approached, seized the earrings and fled. Uttaṅka pursued and caught hold of him. The mendicant, abandoning that form and assuming the form of Takṣaka, suddenly entered a great burrow that opened in the earth.

sanskrit: praviśya ca nāgalokaṃ svabhavanam agacchat tam uttaṅko 'nvāviveśa tenaiva bilena praviśya ca nāgān astuvad ebhiḥ ślokaiḥ
english: Entering the realm of the serpents, he went to his own abode. Uttaṅka followed him through that same burrow, and having entered, he praised the serpents with these verses.

sanskrit: ya airāvatarājānaḥ sarpāḥ samitiśobhanāḥ varṣanta iva jīmūtāḥ savidyutpavaneritāḥ
english: 'Those serpents who are kings descended from Airāvata, resplendent in assembly, like rain-clouds with lightning, stirred by the wind —'

sanskrit: surūpāś ca virūpāś ca tathā kalmāṣakuṇḍalāḥ ādityavan nākapṛṣṭhe rejur airāvatodbhavāḥ
english: '— beautiful and ugly alike, with dappled earrings, those born of Airāvata shone like the sun in the vault of heaven.'

sanskrit: bahūni nāgavartmāni gaṅgāyās tīra uttare icchet ko 'rkāṃśusenāyāṃ cartum airāvataṃ vinā
english: 'Many are the serpent-paths along the northern bank of the Gaṅgā — who would wish to move through the army of the sun's rays without Airāvata?'

sanskrit: śatāny aśītir aṣṭau ca sahasrāṇi ca viṃśatiḥ sarpāṇāṃ pragrahā yānti dhṛtarāṣṭro yad ejati
english: 'Eight hundred and eighty hundreds, and twenty thousands — so many multitudes of serpents proceed forth whenever Dhṛtarāṣṭra stirs.'

sanskrit: ye cainam upasarpanti ye ca dūraṃ paraṃ gatāḥ aham airāvatajyeṣṭhabhrātṛbhyo 'karavaṃ namaḥ
english: 'Those who approach him and those who have gone far beyond — to the elder brothers of Airāvata I have made my obeisance.'

sanskrit: yasya vāsaḥ kurukṣetre khāṇḍave cābhavat sadā taṃ kādraveyam astauṣaṃ kuṇḍalārthāya takṣakam
english: 'Him whose dwelling was always in Kurukṣetra and in the Khāṇḍava forest — that son of Kadrū, Takṣaka, I now praise for the sake of the earrings.'

sanskrit: takṣakaś cāśvasenaś ca nityaṃ sahacarāv ubhau kurukṣetre nivasatāṃ nadīm ikṣumatīm anu
english: 'Takṣaka and Aśvasena, those two who are constant companions, dwell in Kurukṣetra along the river Ikṣumatī.'

sanskrit: jaghanyajas takṣakasya śrutaseneti yaḥ śrutaḥ avasadyo mahad dyumni prārthayan nāgamukhyatām karavāṇi sadā cāhaṃ namas tasmai mahātmane
english: 'The youngest-born of Takṣaka, known as Śrutasena, who is destined to eclipse great glory while seeking the foremost rank among the serpents — to that great-souled one I shall always give reverence.'

sanskrit: evaṃ stuvann api nāgān yadā te kuṇḍale nālabhad athāpaśyat striyau tantre adhiropya paṭaṃ vayantyau
english: Even as he praised the serpents thus, when he still did not obtain the earrings, he then saw two women who, having placed cloth on a loom, were weaving fabric.

sanskrit: tasmiṃś ca tantre kṛṣṇāḥ sitāś ca tantavaḥ cakraṃ cāpaśyat ṣaḍbhiḥ kumāraiḥ parivartyamānam puruṣaṃ cāpaśyad darśanīyam
english: And in that loom were black and white threads. He also saw a wheel being turned by six youths, and he saw a handsome man.

sanskrit: sa tān sarvāṃs tuṣṭāva ebhir mantravādaślokaiḥ
english: He praised all of them with these verses of sacred incantation.

sanskrit: trīṇy arpitāny atra śatāni madhye; ṣaṣṭiś ca nityaṃ carati dhruve 'smin cakre caturviṃśatiparvayoge; ṣaḍ yat kumārāḥ parivartayanti
english: 'Three hundred are set in the middle of it, and sixty move perpetually in this fixed wheel — joined in twenty-four segments — which the six youths turn.'

sanskrit: tantraṃ cedaṃ viśvarūpaṃ yuvatyau; vayatas tantūn satataṃ vartayantyau kṛṣṇān sitāṃś caiva vivartayantyau; bhūtāny ajasraṃ bhuvanāni caiva
english: 'And this loom of universal form — two young women weaving, perpetually drawing out threads, turning the black and white ones unceasingly — all beings and all the worlds are woven upon it.'

sanskrit: vajrasya bhartā bhuvanasya goptā; vṛtrasya hantā namucer nihantā kṛṣṇe vasāno vasane mahātmā; satyānṛte yo vivinakti loke
english: 'The bearer of the thunderbolt, the protector of the worlds, the slayer of Vṛtra, the destroyer of Namuci — that great-souled one who wears dark garments, who distinguishes truth from falsehood in the world —'

sanskrit: yo vājinaṃ garbham apāṃ purāṇaṃ; vaiśvānaraṃ vāhanam abhyupetaḥ namaḥ sadāsmai jagadīśvarāya; lokatrayeśāya puraṃdarāya
english: '— who has mounted the ancient embryo of the waters, the horse, whose vehicle is the fire of Vaiśvānara — homage always to him, the lord of the universe, the ruler of the three worlds, the destroyer of citadels.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa enaṃ puruṣaḥ prāha prīto 'smi te 'ham anena stotreṇa kiṃ te priyaṃ karavāṇīti
english: Then that man said to him: 'I am pleased with you by this hymn of praise. What that is dear to you shall I do?'

sanskrit: sa tam uvāca nāgā me vaśam īyur iti
english: He said to him: 'May the serpents come under my control.'

sanskrit: sa enaṃ puruṣaḥ punar uvāca etam aśvam apāne dhamasveti
english: That man said to him again: 'Blow into the lower aperture of this horse.'

sanskrit: sa tam aśvam apāne 'dhamat athāśvād dhamyamānāt sarvasrotobhyaḥ sadhūmā arciṣo 'gner niṣpetuḥ
english: He blew into the lower aperture of the horse. Then, as the horse was blown into, from all its orifices flames of fire with billowing smoke burst forth.

sanskrit: tābhir nāgaloko dhūpitaḥ
english: By those flames the serpent world was fumigated.

sanskrit: atha sasaṃbhramas takṣako 'gnitejobhayaviṣaṇṇas te kuṇḍale gṛhītvā sahasā svabhavanān niṣkramyottaṅkam uvāca ete kuṇḍale pratigṛhṇātu bhavān iti
english: Then Takṣaka, in great agitation and terrified by the power of the fire, seized the earrings and swiftly emerged from his own abode and said to Uttaṅka: 'Please accept these earrings, reverend sir.'

sanskrit: sa te pratijagrāhottaṅkaḥ kuṇḍale pratigṛhyācintayat adya tat puṇyakam upādhyāyinyāḥ dūraṃ cāham abhyāgataḥ kathaṃ nu khalu saṃbhāvayeyam iti
english: Uttaṅka received those earrings. Having received them he reflected: 'Today is the auspicious day of my teacher's wife, and I have come from far away — how indeed shall I reach her in time?'

sanskrit: tata enaṃ cintayānam eva sa puruṣa uvāca uttaṅka enam aśvam adhiroha eṣa tvāṃ kṣaṇād evopādhyāyakulaṃ prāpayiṣyatīti
english: Then, even as he was thus reflecting, that man said to him: 'Uttaṅka, mount this horse — it will bring you to your teacher's household in a moment.'

sanskrit: sa tathety uktvā tam aśvam adhiruhya pratyājagāmopādhyāyakulam upādhyāyinī ca snātā keśān āvapayanty upaviṣṭottaṅko nāgacchatīti śāpāyāsya mano dadhe
english: Saying 'so be it,' he mounted that horse and returned to his teacher's household. The teacher's wife, having bathed and sitting with her hair being dressed, was about to resolve in her mind to curse Uttaṅka since he had not yet come.

sanskrit: athottaṅkaḥ praviśya upādhyāyinīm abhyavādayat te cāsyai kuṇḍale prāyacchat
english: Then Uttaṅka entered, paid his respects to the teacher's wife, and offered her those earrings.

sanskrit: sā cainaṃ pratyuvāca uttaṅka deśe kāle 'bhyāgataḥ svāgataṃ te vatsa manāg asi mayā na śaptaḥ śreyas tavopasthitam siddhim āpnuhīti
english: She replied to him: 'Uttaṅka, you have arrived at the right place and time. Welcome, dear child. You are only barely not cursed by me. Good fortune attends you — may you attain fulfillment.'

sanskrit: athottaṅka upādhyāyam abhyavādayat tam upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca vatsottaṅka svāgataṃ te kiṃ ciraṃ kṛtam iti
english: Then Uttaṅka paid reverence to his teacher. The teacher replied to him: 'Welcome, dear Uttaṅka. Why were you delayed so long?'

sanskrit: tam uttaṅka upādhyāyaṃ pratyuvāca bhos takṣakeṇa nāgarājena vighnaḥ kṛto 'smin karmaṇi tenāsmi nāgalokaṃ nītaḥ
english: Uttaṅka replied to his teacher: 'Sir, an obstruction was caused in this undertaking by Takṣaka, king of the serpents — he carried me off to the serpent world.'

sanskrit: tatra ca mayā dṛṣṭe striyau tantre 'dhiropya paṭaṃ vayantyau tasmiṃś ca tantre kṛṣṇāḥ sitāś ca tantavaḥ kiṃ tat
english: 'There I saw two women who, having placed cloth upon a loom, were weaving, with black and white threads in that loom — what does that signify?'

sanskrit: tatra ca mayā cakraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ dvādaśāram ṣaṭ cainaṃ kumārāḥ parivartayanti tad api kim
english: 'There too I saw a wheel with twelve spokes, and six youths turning it — what does that signify as well?'

sanskrit: puruṣaś cāpi mayā dṛṣṭaḥ sa punaḥ kaḥ
english: 'And I also saw a man — who then is he?'

sanskrit: aśvaś cātipramāṇayuktaḥ sa cāpi kaḥ
english: 'And a horse of extraordinary size — who is that also?'

sanskrit: pathi gacchatā mayā ṛṣabho dṛṣṭaḥ taṃ ca puruṣo 'dhirūḍhaḥ tenāsmi sopacāram uktaḥ uttaṅkāsya ṛṣabhasya purīṣaṃ bhakṣaya upādhyāyenāpi te bhakṣitam iti tatas tadvacanān mayā tadṛṣabhasya purīṣam upayuktam tad icchāmi bhavatopadiṣṭaṃ kiṃ tad iti
english: 'While going along the path I saw a great bull, and a man was mounted upon it. That man addressed me with courtesy: "Uttaṅka, eat the dung of this bull — your teacher has also eaten it." Then, upon his word, I consumed the dung of that bull. I wish to know what all of this means as explained by you.'

sanskrit: tenaivam ukta upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca ye te striyau dhātā vidhātā ca ye ca te kṛṣṇāḥ sitāś ca tantavas te rātryahanī
english: Addressed thus, the teacher replied: 'Those two women are Dhātā and Vidhātā; those black and white threads are night and day.'

sanskrit: yad api tac cakraṃ dvādaśāraṃ ṣaṭ kumārāḥ parivartayanti te ṛtavaḥ ṣaṭ saṃvatsaraś cakram yaḥ puruṣaḥ sa parjanyaḥ yo 'śvaḥ so 'gniḥ
english: 'That wheel with twelve spokes that the six youths turn — those six are the seasons, and the wheel is the year. The man is Parjanya, the rain-god; the horse is Agni, the fire.'

sanskrit: ya ṛṣabhas tvayā pathi gacchatā dṛṣṭaḥ sa airāvato nāgarājaḥ yaś cainam adhirūḍhaḥ sa indraḥ yad api te purīṣaṃ bhakṣitaṃ tasya ṛṣabhasya tad amṛtam
english: 'That bull you saw as you went along the path — that is Airāvata, king of the serpents. He who was mounted upon it is Indra. And that dung of the bull that you consumed — that is ambrosia, the nectar of immortality.'

sanskrit: tena khalv asi na vyāpannas tasmin nāgabhavane sa cāpi mama sakhā indraḥ
english: 'It is by that that you were not destroyed in that serpent abode. And Indra is also my friend.'

sanskrit: tadanugrahāt kuṇḍale gṛhītvā punar abhyāgato 'si tat saumya gamyatām anujāne bhavantam śreyo 'vāpsyasīti
english: 'By his grace you have returned having obtained the earrings. So, gentle one, you may go — I give you leave. You shall attain great good fortune.'

sanskrit: sa upādhyāyenānujñāta uttaṅkaḥ kruddhas takṣakasya praticikīrṣamāṇo hāstinapuraṃ pratasthe
english: Given leave by his teacher, Uttaṅka, filled with anger and determined to retaliate against Takṣaka, set out for the city of Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: sa hāstinapuraṃ prāpya nacirād dvijasattamaḥ samāgacchata rājānam uttaṅko janamejayam
english: That foremost brahmin Uttaṅka, reaching Hāstinapura before long, came to meet King Janamejaya.

sanskrit: purā takṣaśilātas taṃ nivṛttam aparājitam samyag vijayinaṃ dṛṣṭvā samantān mantribhir vṛtam
english: He saw him just returned from Takṣaśilā, undefeated, fully victorious, and attended on all sides by his ministers.

sanskrit: tasmai jayāśiṣaḥ pūrvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ prayujya saḥ uvācainaṃ vacaḥ kāle śabdasaṃpannayā girā
english: Having first offered him the customary blessings of victory, he addressed the king at the proper moment with words adorned with eloquent speech.

sanskrit: anyasmin karaṇīye tvaṃ kārye pārthivasattama bālyād ivānyad eva tvaṃ kuruṣe nṛpasattama
english: 'While there is another duty to be done, O best of kings, you attend to something altogether different, as if out of childishness, O foremost of monarchs.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tu vipreṇa sa rājā pratyuvāca ha janamejayaḥ prasannātmā samyak saṃpūjya taṃ munim
english: Addressed thus by the brahmin, King Janamejaya replied, his mind serene, having duly honoured that sage.

sanskrit: āsāṃ prajānāṃ paripālanena; svaṃ kṣatradharmaṃ paripālayāmi prabrūhi vā kiṃ kriyatāṃ dvijendra; śuśrūṣur asmy adya vacas tvadīyam
english: 'I protect my own warrior-dharma through the protection of these subjects. Or tell me, what is to be done, O lord among brahmins — today I am eager to hear your words.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktas tu nṛpottamena; dvijottamaḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ uvāca rājānam adīnasattvaṃ; svam eva kāryaṃ nṛpateś ca yat tat
english: Addressed thus by that best of kings, the foremost brahmin, the most excellent among the meritorious, spoke to the king of undaunted spirit concerning the very duty that was the king's own.

sanskrit: takṣakeṇa narendrendra yena te hiṃsitaḥ pitā tasmai pratikuruṣva tvaṃ pannagāya durātmane
english: 'O lord among lords of men, retaliate against that serpent of evil soul, Takṣaka, by whom your father was slain.'

sanskrit: kāryakālaṃ ca manye 'haṃ vidhidṛṣṭasya karmaṇaḥ tad gacchāpacitiṃ rājan pitus tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: 'And I consider this the proper time for the action enjoined by sacred ordinance. Therefore go, O king, and perform the act of vengeance for that great-souled father of yours.'

sanskrit: tena hy anaparādhī sa daṣṭo duṣṭāntarātmanā pañcatvam agamad rājā vajrāhata iva drumaḥ
english: 'For that king, though guiltless, was bitten by that one of wicked inner soul and passed away to the five elements, like a tree struck by a thunderbolt.'
